title: South Korea Visa Services Expand to Four Indian Cities via VFS
excerpt: VFS Global opened a new Korea Visa Application Centre in New Delhi on September 15, bringing its South Asia network to six centres — four in India plus Dhaka and Colombo — as demand for South Korea travel keeps climbing.
body:
• VFS Global opened a new Korea Visa Application Centre in New Delhi on September 15, 2026, inaugurated by South Korean Ambassador to India Lee Seong-ho.
  • The four Indian centres — New Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai and Kolkata — are part of a network of six across South Asia, alongside new centres in Dhaka and Colombo.
  • The centres handle visiting, business, tourist, short-term employment, student, research and dependent visa applications; VFS handles paperwork and biometrics only, while Korean diplomatic authorities make the visa decisions.
  • The expansion answers rising demand for South Korea travel among Indians, driven by tourism, education, business and the growing pull of Korean popular culture.

New Delhi gets a dedicated Korea visa centre

Indian travellers bound for South Korea have a new place to start their journey. VFS Global inaugurated a Korea Visa Application Centre in New Delhi on September 15, 2026, taking its South Korea visa footprint to six centres across South Asia, according to the Hindu Businessline.

The New Delhi centre, located at Shivaji Stadium Metro Station in Connaught Place, was opened by H.E. Lee Seong-ho, Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to India. It joins existing centres in Bengaluru, Chennai and Kolkata, alongside newly opened centres in Dhaka, Bangladesh, and Colombo, Sri Lanka. Globally, VFS Global now manages nine Korea visa centres across six countries.

According to Travel Span, the centres accept applications across a wide range of categories: visiting, business, tourist, short-term employment, student, research and dependent visas. VFS Global's role is limited to the administrative front end — collecting application forms and supporting documents as per the checklist, and enrolling biometrics. It has no role in the decision-making process; granting or refusing a visa remains the sole prerogative of the concerned Korean Embassy.

Context & Background

VFS Global has handled South Korea visa processing in India since 2011, so this is an expansion rather than a debut. The centres promise upgraded facilities and trained staff to make applications more convenient, according to the Hindu Businessline.

The New Delhi centre sits on the mezzanine level of Shivaji Stadium Metro Station on Baba Kharak Singh Marg in Connaught Place. Bengaluru's is at Gopalan Innovation Mall on Bannerghatta Main Road in J.P. Nagar; Chennai's is at Ramee Mall on Anna Salai in Teynampet; Kolkata's is at Rene Tower on Rajdanga Main Road in Kasba.

The timing lines up with VFS Global's 25th anniversary. The company, headquartered in Zurich and Dubai and majority-owned by Blackstone, operates more than 4,200 application centres across 170 countries, has processed over 562 million transactions since 2001, and serves 71 client governments, according to the Hindu Businessline.

Impact & Analysis

The driver, in VFS Global's own telling, is demand. Yummi Talwar, Chief Operating Officer for South Asia, cited growing visa demand across the region as the reason for the expansion. South Korea's popularity among Indian travellers has been climbing, with Seoul, Busan and Jeju Island drawing more visitors, and Korean popular culture — K-pop, television dramas and films — fuelling interest among younger Indians, according to Saptashwa TV.

The geography of the network matters. Four Indian metros means applicants in the national capital, the south and the east can submit closer to home, while the Dhaka and Colombo additions knit the region's growing Korea-bound traffic into a single system. Business travel is part of the equation too: commercial, educational and cultural ties between South Korea and India keep generating trips for meetings, conferences and study, not just tourism.

"This is an important step in further strengthening the relationship between the Republic of Korea and India. The new centre has been designed to provide applicants with a seamless, efficient, and accessible application experience."

— Lee Seong-ho, Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to India

"Reaching six Korea Visa Application Centres across three countries in South Asia is a significant milestone in our partnership with the Republic of Korea and reflects the growing demand for Korea visas among travellers across the region."

— Yummi Talwar, Chief Operating Officer – South Asia, VFS Global

Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora, the expansion is mostly about convenience and momentum: families with relatives in India planning Korea trips, students eyeing Korean universities, and professionals shuttling between Indian and Korean business hubs all get a shorter path to the application window.

What's Next

Applicants still need to check the fine print before visiting a centre: visa category, documentation requirements, appointment procedures, processing timelines and fees can all vary by purpose and length of travel. VFS Global's South Korea portal for India carries the checklists and appointment details. With Korean travel interest still rising, the bet here is that the new centres will fill up fast — and the real test will be whether upgraded facilities and trained staff translate into shorter, smoother processing for applicants.
